source_issue: Seven declarations use the element-mapping arrow in expressions that state only a function's domain and codomain, repeating the determined notation issue in earlier lectures.
target_action: Preserved the printed mapsto arrows in the English semantic witness, normalized them to right arrows in the learner-facing Indonesian type declarations, and disclosed the correction in the edition notice.

surface: Monotonic behavior along a recession direction
source_issue: The source says the function is monotonically nondecreasing along a direction that keeps every sublevel set invariant; the epigraph definition and the neighboring six-case diagram require monotonically nonincreasing behavior.
target_action: Preserved 'monotonically nondecreasing' in the English witness, rendered the learner-facing statement as monotonically nonincreasing (tak-menaik), and disclosed the semantic reversal.

surface: Direction symbol below the six descent-behavior panels
source_issue: The source says y is a recession direction in panels (a)-(d), although the panels and all surrounding definitions use d as the direction variable.
target_action: Preserved y in the English witness, used d in the learner-facing Indonesian edition, and disclosed the determined symbol correction.

surface: Set-builder expression connecting the function recession cone to the epigraph recession cone
source_issue: The printed expression R_f = {(d,0) in R_epi(f)} omits the bound variable and set-builder separator, so its right-hand side is a set of pairs rather than a set of directions.
target_action: Preserved the malformed expression in the English witness and wrote R_f={d | (d,0) in R_epi(f)} in the learner-facing edition, with an explicit correction note.

source_issue: The source introduces an epsilon-neighborhood in the local-minimizer definition without quantifying epsilon or requiring it to be positive.
target_action: Preserved the unquantified epsilon in the English witness and added 'for some epsilon greater than zero' to the learner-facing definition, with disclosure.

surface: Feasibility in the extended Weierstrass theorem
source_issue: The theorem's bounded-X alternative does not state that X intersects dom f; without feasibility the asserted nonempty minimizer set can fail even when X is closed and bounded.
target_action: Preserved the printed theorem in the English witness and added X intersect dom f nonempty to the learner-facing theorem, matching the explicit feasibility convention on page 60 and the convex specialization on page 62.

surface: Proof shorthand for constrained sublevel sets
source_issue: The proof calls the relevant objects 'level sets of f intersect X', which is not a well-formed function or set construction and obscures that the sets are constrained sublevel sets.
target_action: Preserved the shorthand in the English witness and wrote the constrained sublevel sets {x in X | f(x) <= gamma} explicitly in the learner-facing proof, with disclosure.

surface: Distinction between a minimizing point and the minimum value
source_issue: The source repeatedly calls a point x-star a minimum and calls collections of such points sets of minima; in particular, the uniqueness statement on page 63 intends a unique minimizer rather than the tautological uniqueness of a minimum value.
target_action: Preserved the printed terminology in the English witness and consistently distinguished titik peminimum from nilai minimum in the learner-facing Indonesian edition, with disclosure.
